title: Do They Do as They Are Told? Investigating Coding Agents' Adherence to Explicit Instructions in Context Files
abstract: arXiv:2611.13709v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Developers increasingly rely on agent context files (ACFs), persistent, project-scoped artifacts such as AGENTS.md, to steer the behavior of autonomous coding agents without renegotiating expectations at every interaction. Yet this governance mechanism rests on an untested assumption: that instructions written into an ACF are actually carried out, rather than ignored or loosely followed. Existing studies describe what ACFs contain, but not whether individual instructions are followed, leaving open which guidance can be trusted. We address this gap through an empirical study of real-world ACF snapshots and their linked agent-generated commits: characterizing the explicit, actionable instructions ACFs encode, operationalizing them into executable measurement scripts, and using these scripts to assess instruction-level compliance. We find that most observable instructions can be operationalized and that agents follow ACF guidance more often

translated_title: 他们是否照章办事？研究编码智能体对上下文文件中明确指令的遵循程度
translated_abstract: 开发人员越来越依赖智能体上下文文件（ACF）——例如 AGENTS.md 这类持久化、项目范围的人为工件——来引导自主编码智能体的行为，而无需在每次交互时重新协商预期。然而，这种治理机制建立在一个未经检验的假设之上：写入 ACF 的指令实际上会被执行，而不是被忽略或被松散地遵循。现有研究只描述了 ACF 包含哪些内容，却没有研究具体指令是否被遵循，因而无法确定哪些指导值得信赖。我们通过对真实世界 ACF 快照及其关联的智能体生成提交的实证研究来填补这一空白：刻画 ACF 中编码的明确且可操作的指令，将其操作化为可执行的测量脚本，并利用这些脚本评估指令级别的合规性。我们发现，大多数可观察的指令都可以被操作化，并且智能体在更多情况下会遵循 ACF 的指导。
tldr: 该研究首次实证检验了编码智能体是否真正执行 AGENTS.md 等智能体上下文文件中的明确指令，通过将指令操作化为可执行测量脚本来量化评估指令级合规性。
en_tdlr: This study empirically investigates whether coding agents actually adhere to explicit instructions in agent context files like AGENTS.md by operationalizing them into executable measurement scripts to assess instruction-level compliance.
